question.problem: For the function $f(x,y),$ calculate $\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y}$ given that $\frac{∂f}{∂y}={x}^{2}y\operatorname{cos}⁡(x{y}^{2}).$
question.worked_solution:
To find $\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y}$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative $\frac{∂f}{∂y}$ with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{∂f}{∂y}) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}y\operatorname{cos}⁡(x{y}^{2})) \\  & =y\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x{y}^{2})) \\  & =y\cdot (2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x{y}^{2})-{x}^{2}{y}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x{y}^{2})) \\  & =2xy\operatorname{cos}⁡(x{y}^{2})-{x}^{2}{y}^{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x{y}^{2})\end{aligned}
$$
